To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the drug resistance mutant of the proton transporter M2 has a different conformation in the transmembrane domain than the wild-type protein, but the drug does not appear to bind to the mutant protein.
the S31N M(2) mutant of the influenza virus proton channel is dimeric and that the mutant is resistant to the drug rimantadine.

the drug-resistant S-31N M2(18 - 60) tetramers assemble as a dimer-of-dimers, as predicted by the X-ray crystal structure of the S31N M-2 protein, and the key resistance residue, S-31, has a different torsional angle than in wild-type M2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural characterization of the drug resistant mutant S31N of M2(23-54).

the development of new NMR techniques to study membrane proteins, including the use of magic-angle spinning to improve the sensitivity and resolution, and the use of ZF-TEDORA RFDR to transfer magnetization through the membrane.
the structural and functional analysis of the proton channel M2 from the influenza A virus, which is essential for the viral replication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the S31N mutant has a different conformational state compared with wild-type M2.
the drug-resistant M2(18/60) is structurally different from the wild-type M2 and the drug does not appear to bind to the mutant.

the NMR spectra are consistent with a model in which the drug binds at a site that is different in the wild-type and the mutant protein, and that the mutant is resistant because it has a different helix structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the S31N mutation disrupts the binding of rimantadine to the channel.
the S31N mutation does not affect the overall structure of M2, but does alter the conformation of the helices, and that rimantadine binding does not occur.
the NMR chemical shifts for the S31N M31 mutant of M2 are similar to the wild type but the drug does not interact with the channel, as expected.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the (15)N ZF-TEDORA RFDR experiment is a powerful approach for obtaining high-quality MAS NMR assignments of membrane proteins.
the S31N mutant is not a simple point mutation that disrupts the wild-type structure and that the drug resistance mechanism is not simply a change in the helix conformation.
MAS-NMR is a powerful tool for the characterization of membrane proteins, even those as large as the M2 proton channel.
